subject: Neo Dynamics — on‑prem SOW & operational clarifications
messages:
From: Alex Moretti <alex.moretti@neodynamics.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@neodynamics.com
Date: 2028-07-15T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Neo Dynamics RFP — clarifications on on‑prem SOW items

Soojín / Ben,

Thanks for the quick intake call this morning. Procurement asked us to capture a few clarifications in writing so they can reconcile with our SOW template (attached). Two specific items we need vendor confirmation on before we proceed to the technical workshop: 

1) Operator access model: will Redwood require a persistent operator account in the customer VPC, or can all maintenance be done via ephemeral operator sessions initiated by the customer's operators?
2) Patch workflow and attestation: for air‑gapped mode, do you provide signed patch bundles and a verification checklist we can onboard into our change control?
3) Telemetry and logs: what telemetry (metrics/traces) leaves the on‑prem environment under the default configuration? Can we opt into zero‑egress telemetry while still getting oncall/alerting?
4) Maintenance windows & SLA credits: outline your proposed maintenance cadence and how emergency security patches are rolled out for isolated instances.

Can you reply with short, SOW‑friendly responses and attach any sample SOW language you typically include? Procurement prefers one consolidated PDF.

Appreciate it — looking forward to the workshop next week.

— Alex
Neo Dynamics
Attachments: Neo_SOW_Template_20280715.docx
From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moretti <alex.moretti@neodynamics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, procurement@neodynamics.com
Date: 2028-07-15T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Neo Dynamics RFP — clarifications on on‑prem SOW items

Alex — thanks for the clear list. I consolidated answers below to align with SOW language; attaching a one‑page PDF we use for procurement and a short appendix with operational notes. If you want, we can convert any of the bullets directly into your SOW template.

Summary (SOW‑friendly):
- Operator access model: Redwood supports a customer‑managed operator model only — no persistent Redwood service accounts are required within the VPC. All vendor maintenance is performed via ephemeral operator sessions initiated by the customer's operators. Sessions are brokered through a jump host and require MFA and ephemeral key material. (See appendix section A: Operator access flows.)
- Patch workflow & attestation (air‑gapped): For isolated deployments we publish signed patch bundles (PGP signed manifest + checksums) and a patch verification checklist. Customer CI/CD or airgap file transfer processes ingest bundles; Redwood provides a patch manifest and MD5/SHA signatures for attestation. We can include a clause that requires vendor to provide signed bundles and a quarterly SBOM snapshot.
- Telemetry & logs: Default installation sends only health pings and aggregated token/usage counters to the customer‑controlled telemetry collector (no customer data or model inputs are exfiltrated). For customers requiring zero‑egress, we support a zero‑egress mode: all telemetry is stored locally and a local alerting bridge runs inside the VPC forwarding alerts to customer endpoints (email/webhook) without leaving the network. We will include a gating checklist for zero‑egress activation.
- Maintenance cadence & emergency patches: Regular maintenance windows are quarterly by default; customers may opt into monthly security-only maintenance. Emergency security patches are made available as signed bundles and a hotfix runbook; Redwood will support a remote guided run with the customer's operators. SLA credits: we are open to a negotiated credit schedule tied to Dedicated support tiers; for Private (on‑prem) customers our baseline is a 99.5% availability commitment for the service control plane, with operational SLAs specified in the SOW addendum.

Attachments: redwood-onprem-answers-v1.pdf (consolidated answers), Neo_RFP_Questions_20280715.pdf (your template with our inline comments).

Suggested next step: we can convert the bullets to SOW clauses and send a prelim SOW ahead of the technical workshop. If that works, I can loop Ben and Marissa for pricing & operational commitments.

Best,
Soojín Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Attachments: redwood-onprem-answers-v1.pdf
From: Alex Moretti <alex.moretti@neodynamics.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@neodynamics.com
Date: 2028-07-16T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Neo Dynamics RFP — clarifications on on‑prem SOW items

Soojín — that is extremely helpful, thanks. A couple of follow‑ups for SOW language and our security team: 

• Can you provide the exact operator session lifecycle steps you expect us to run? We want the step‑by‑step so it maps to our control objectives (create session, approve via MFA, apply changes, session revoke, audit log extraction).
• For the zero‑egress telemetry option, does Redwood still require outbound DNS resolution to validate signatures or check CRLs for patch bundles, or can the install be fully air‑gapped (no DNS/eph egress) if we host a local CRL and signature verifier?
• For SLA credits, procurement wants an example credit table and the blackout periods where maintenance is allowed without credit — can you add a paragraph to the SOW draft that shows those numbers?

If you can attach a preliminary SOW with those items addressed, procurement will review and then we'll schedule a short 30‑minute pricing and legal session.

— Alex
Attachments: —
From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-17T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal — Neo Dynamics SOW inputs (operator lifecycle / SLA table / pricing)

Ben / Marissa — routing Neo Dynamics procurement follow‑ups. Key asks to cover in the prelim SOW: 

1) Operator session lifecycle — they want a step‑by‑step sequence for their control audit. I have a draft (see appendix in our answers PDF) but need the formal runbook language and any required tooling notes (e.g., jump host, MFA provider, session TTLs).
2) Air‑gapped verification — security wants an explicit statement that Redwood's patch signature verification can be run entirely offline if customer hosts the signature verifier and CRL; confirm any contract points around support scope for offline verification.
3) SLA credits table & blackout periods — procurement asked for an example table. We should present two options: Standard Private (99.5% control plane, quarterly maintenance, example credits) and Enterprise Private (99.8% control plane, monthly security patches, expanded on‑call).

Suggested owner: Ben — prelim SOW & credit table; Marissa — pricing tiers and acceptance criteria. Target: send prelim SOW back to Alex by 2028‑07‑20 so procurement can review before the technical workshop (2028‑07‑25).

Also flagging legal items: customer prefers no persistent vendor accounts. We already stated ephemeral operator sessions — confirm that the SOW includes a binding clause stating no vendor persistent credentials are provisioned in customer VPC.

Thanks — Soh
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moretti <alex.moretti@neodynamics.com>, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, procurement@neodynamics.com
Date: 2028-07-20T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Neo Dynamics RFP — prelim SOW and example credit table

Alex / Soh — attaching a preliminary SOW that incorporates the operator lifecycle steps, an SLA credit table, and air‑gap support language. High level notes inside the document: 

• Operator lifecycle: sections 3.1‑3.4 show the flow we recommend (operator requests session via customer portal -> customer operator performs MFA -> ephemeral key minted for session -> changes executed under operator user -> session revocation and signed audit export). We explicitly call out that Redwood will not provision persistent vendor accounts; all vendor support is performed via guided ephemeral sessions when requested by customer operators.
• Air‑gapped verification: section 4.2 includes an offline verification option. Redwood provides PGP signed artifacts and a local verifier package; customers can run verification without outbound DNS/CRL calls by hosting CRL and package metadata locally. Our support scope for offline verification is limited to remote guidance and runbook support unless an elevated support engagement is purchased.
• SLA credits & blackout: attached table shows Standard vs Enterprise Private options with sample credits (0.5% credit for each 0.5% below SLA up to 5%). Quarterly maintenance windows are default; Enterprise option offers monthly security windows with increased support.

Attachment: prelim-sow-neodynamics-20280720.docx (prelim SOW + credit table).

If this looks good we can finalize language with legal and route to DocuSign. Also happy to run the technical workshop and walk the customer through sections 3 and 4.

Best,
Ben Carter
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
